blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by a red border only) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. A screen reader user who tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing: no text, no `aria-invalid`, no message, so they cannot tell which field is wrong and cannot complete checkout; a colour-blind user cannot tell the red border from the grey one. Add a text message under each invalid field, associated with it through `aria-describedby`, set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, and keep the red border only as a supplement (an icon helps too). Update the spec's scenarios ("the field's border turns red" / "returns to grey") to require the message and its association, and task 1.2 to verify them.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by a red border only

findings.evidence: - The error list at the top of the form is removed.
findings.recommendation: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 4.1.3 Status Messages. A keyboard or screen reader user who submits without having left every field (so blur validation never ran on them) or who missed the inline state gets no list, no announcement and no focus move: pressing Enter on submit does nothing they can perceive. The plan says nothing of submit behaviour once the summary is gone. Specify that on submit with invalid fields, focus moves to the first invalid field (or to a kept, linked error summary), and its message is announced; add a scenario for it in the spec.
findings.title: Removing the error summary leaves submit with no announced errors or focus target
